entries.alt: Jesus rises above an olive-covered hillside, looking tenderly down toward the disciples watching Him.
entries.caption: As the disciples watch, Jesus is taken up and a cloud receives Him. This picture interprets the moment of parting; His tender downward gaze, the arrangement of the gathering and the surrounding landscape are artistic choices.
findings: The revised face turns down and left toward the gathered disciples. Chin is lowered, lips closed without exposed teeth or the rejected broad upward smile. The mood is restrained, affectionate and appropriate to parting.
Canonical Christ brow, nose, beard, hair and face remain recognizable through the changed angle and expression. Lifelike skin, fabric and daylight; no painterly face or theatrical grin.
Elevated feet and cloud communicate Ascension; onlookers look upward toward Him. Arms, visible hands and fingers trace coherently. Small healed palm/wrist marks are visible, without fresh wounds.

Caption must describe an interpretation rather than claim His exact emotion, pose, roster of witnesses, modern archaeological location or the complete sequence. The two men in white of Acts 1:10 are not depicted; do not claim they are.
This technical review finds the requested expression correction satisfied; it is not a claim of Wyatt’s approval of the revision.

entries.alt: A man studies his restored hand while Jesus watches him with calm attention inside a synagogue.
entries.caption: Jesus asks the man to stretch out his hand, and it is restored. The picture shows him considering his hand after that response; his appearance and the synagogue furnishings are interpreted.
findings: The hand is visibly ordinary and functional rather than malformed; use an after-restoration caption, not a caption claiming this is the still-withered hand.
Christ’s canonical identity remains recognizable, with attentive subdued expression and gaze toward the man. The man looks at his hand, a meaningful scene-specific response.
Foreground hand/forearm and visible face anatomy are coherent. Skin, beard and period cloth retain photographic detail; no forced miracle glow, blood or pre-Resurrection nail scars.

Background watchers and synagogue objects are interpreted, not identified named opponents or verified room reconstruction. The image illustrates the restoring result, not the preceding look of anger/grief at hardened hearts.

entries.alt: Jesus takes an older woman by the hand and helps her rise from bedding as they look toward one another.
entries.caption: In Simon’s home, Jesus takes Simon’s mother-in-law by the hand and lifts her up. Mark records that the fever leaves her and she begins to serve. Her age, appearance and the room’s details are artistic interpretation.
findings: Hand contact and the woman’s rising posture follow the narrated action. Their reciprocal gaze and relief suit the healing moment; the smile is directed at her, not at the viewer.
Christ’s approved identity is recognizable. Hands at the clasp belong to the two visible arms; legs and feet fit their positions and the bedding. No definite duplicated or detached anatomy detected.
The other Christ arm extends behind her shoulder; no claim is made about an unseen hand. The visible domestic materials and natural light remain plausible interpretation.

Do not identify the background man as Peter, Andrew, James or John from pixels alone; no particular disciple identity reference is established for him. Do not imply service is a condition for receiving healing.

entries.alt: Two messengers speak with Jesus on a village street, one gesturing toward a nearby home.
entries.caption: The centurion sends friends to Jesus with his message of trust: a word from Him is enough. This illustrates Luke’s account of the messengers; the centurion and the sick servant are outside the frame.
findings: The two civilian speakers, rather than an armored centurion addressing Christ personally, fit Luke’s messenger account. Caption must keep that distinction.
Christ’s face matches the approved identity with serious listening rather than generic smile. Messenger eye lines and the open pointing gesture support the conversation.

Foreground clasped hands, visible gesturing hand, faces and cloth are coherent; no obvious extra fingers or detached limbs. Village architecture and scaffold-like background timber are reconstructed surroundings.
The distant figures must remain unnamed. Do not claim the servant’s actual recovery is pictured or assign a definite house location.

entries.alt: A woman reaches from behind to touch Jesus’s outer garment as He turns amid the crowd.
entries.caption: The woman reaches through the crowd and touches Jesus’s clothing. Mark describes Him turning to ask who touched Him. Her position, expression and the precise fold of cloth are interpreted; the picture does not yet show their later face-to-face conversation.
findings: The woman contacts the outer garment from behind. Christ turns and looks across the surrounding crowd, not directly into her eyes; this fits the immediate searching/questioning moment in verse 30.
Canonical Christ face remains clear through the turned head. The woman’s attentive, hopeful expression and modest dress avoid sensationalizing her illness.

Her hand meets cloth naturally, and Christ’s hanging hand has coherent fingers and wrist. No visible healed nail scars in this mortal scene. Foreground crowd occlusion is natural rather than unexplained missing anatomy.

Use clothing/garment rather than claiming a specific lower hem edge in this Mark-based image. Do not add visible blood, a medical diagnosis beyond the record, or a claim that touching fabric mechanically guarantees healing.

entries.alt: Jesus holds a blind man’s hand and leads him away from the village along a stony path.
entries.caption: At Bethsaida, Jesus takes the blind man by the hand and leads him out of the town before healing him. The guiding walk is the moment shown; the man’s appearance and the town’s exact setting are interpreted.
findings: The town is behind the pair and their linked hands make the leading action clear. This is distinct from an eye-touch healing image and should stay captioned as the walk before the healing.

Christ looks attentively toward the man with recognizable canonical face and quiet concern. The man’s closed eyes and cautious reaching arm communicate the interpreted need for guidance without grotesque disability portrayal.

Contact hands have coherent overlapping fingers and traceable arms. The free hands, heads and legs are anatomically plausible. Detailed skin, cloth and natural surroundings meet the requested photographic character.
No nail scars or invented magic are visible. Do not imply closed eyes establish a medical presentation shared by all blind people or that the picture shows completed restored sight.

review_scope: Independent direct full-image pixel review of the six supplied generated PNGs, compared with actual canonical Christ pixels. Source events checked against previously verified official passages. No owner approval inferred; no phone/browser rendering pass claimed.
